The Court Made The Following:
 Order

The petitioner-accused No.1 is before this Court seeking grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.,
in Crime No.481/2022 of Ramamurthy Nagar Police Station, Bengaluru registered for the offences punishable under Sections 376. 366(A) read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC')
and Sections 4 and 6 of POCSO Act and Sections 9, 10 and 11 of Prohibition of Child Marriage Act on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant - Smt.Mehar Taj.
2.
Heard Sri. Syed Akbar Pasha, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. K.Rahul Rai, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.
Perused the materials on record.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is arrayed as accused No.1.
He is innocent and has not committed any offences as alleged.
He has been falsely implicated in the matter without any basis.
He was apprehended on 19.11.2022 and since then he is in judicial custody.
Learned counsel further submitted that it is the case made out by the prosecution that the petitioner married the victim girl on 05.04.2021 and she delivered a baby girl on 13.11.2022.
Since it is alleged that the petitioner had already married the victim girl, the offences punishable under POCSO Act are not made out.
The investigation is completed and the charge sheet is filed.
The petitioner is not having any criminal antecedents.
He is not required to be detained in custody for any other purpose except to ensure his presence before the trial Court.
He is the permanent resident of the address mentioned in the cause-title to the petition and is ready and willing to abide by any of the conditions that would be imposed by this Court.
Hence, he prays to allow the petition.
4. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader opposing the petition submitted that serious allegations are made against the petitioner for having committed the offences.
The victim girl was aged 16 years and the petitioner had married her and committed penetrative sexual assault as a result of which she gave birth to baby girl on 13.11.2022.
When the birth certificate of victim girl is produced by her mother, it was found that the victim girl was a minor.
The investigation is completed and the charge sheet is filed.
There are strong prima-facie materials against the petitioner for having committed the aforesaid offences.

Looking to the nature and seriousness of the offence,

sentences.text: the petitioner is not entitled for grant of bail.
If he is enlarged on bail, there is every chance of influencing and threatening the victim girl to dissuade from giving evidence.
Hence, he prays for dismissal of the petition.

5. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Negative' for the following:
REASONS 6.
Serious allegations are made against the petitioner for having committed the offences.
The petitioner married the minor girl who was hardly aged 16 years.
It is stated that date of birth of the victim girl is on 15.02.2005 and she delivered a baby girl on 13.11.2022 when she was still a minor.
After investigating the matter, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet with necessary documents, which prima-facie disclose commission of the offence by the petitioner.

If at this stage,
the petitioner is enlarged on bail, there is every chance of he influencing and threatening the victim girl and dissuading her from deposing before the Court.

Looking to the nature and seriousness of the offence and materials collected by the Investigating Officer to prove the commission of offence, the petitioner is not entitled for grant of bail.
7.

Accordingly, I answer the above point in the negative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is dismissed.
